artboards.title: E · A plot, and its guest book

annotations.text:
Five organising principles for the phase-2 shared garden, not five layouts.
Each answers "what is a garden of four thousand plants FOR" differently.
Vocabulary lifted from Chrome.swift, docs/BRAND.md and design/*.dc.html: ground #0D0D1F, white at 100/55/28/16%, 11px tracked-2.4 uppercase labels, italic serif plant names, hairline rules.
Plants are hand-drawn stand-ins — the real screen derives geometry from the seed on the viewer's own device.

A · Meadow — density and place. Best wonder, worst findability. Hard on the web without WebGL.
B · Lineage — says what the app IS: a record of meetings. Ports natively to a wide screen. Weak when your own plant has no descendants yet.
C · Herbarium — findable, sortable, archival. The one that survives four thousand plants. Least feeling.
D · Path — the existing stage screen, made continuous. Truest to the app's register. One plant at a time is slow at scale.
E · Plot — the actual social surface, and the one that brings reporting, blocking and moderation with it.

The web port is C's data with D's hero. A public plant page is what gets shared into a group chat, so it has to carry the whole story above the fold — name, passage, both gardeners, place, generation.
One open question: whether a public page shows both names, or only the one who chose to share.
